prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: deepseek-flash (served at api.deepseek.com).
Game: Don't Starve.
About the game: Don't Starve is a real-time survival and crafting game with continuous survival rather than a finite ending in this setting. A trial starts Wilson in an undeveloped first-day base-game world with DLC disabled and the official Long Day option, retaining a day/dusk/night cycle. The trial's frozen rubric defines the native-day target and milestones. Only continuous survival within one episode earns points; optional crafting earns no points. Death may start a fresh language-model episode within the original budget; Jev ends at its first death. This setting does not measure Adventure Mode completion.
Controls:
W/A/S/D move. Space performs a nearby contextual action. F attacks a nearby target. Left click performs the primary action at the pointer. Right click performs the secondary action at the pointer; the current typed-choice profile cannot express right clicks. Escape opens or closes menus, Tab toggles the map, Q/E rotate the camera, and Return confirms menu selections. Scroll changes zoom or scrolls the visible interface. These are ordinary input bindings, not a strategy. Number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate the native action for items in inventory slots 1 through 10. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
Choose one ordinary keyboard, left-click or scroll input using the screenshot. Keyboard inputs are held for 3 seconds. Coordinates are normalized: (0, 0) is the upper-left corner and (1, 1) the lower-right corner. Grid clicks use 10 rows and 18 columns: x=(column+0.5)/18, y=(row+0.5)/10. Left-edge targets use x=0.015625 and y=(row+0.5)/14 for rows 0 through 13. Bottom-edge targets use x=(column+0.5)/24 for columns 0 through 23 and y=0.958333. The center target is (0.5, 0.5). The profile describes controls only and provides no game objectives. The number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate inventory slots 1 through 10 using the native inventory action for the item in that slot. Hovering an inventory item displays its native action label. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
Group action: Select one input. The chosen key combination, left click or scroll is executed as a single action.
  up: Hold W to move up. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the previous category.
  left: Hold A to move left. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the previous entry.
  down: Hold S to move down. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the next category.
  right: Hold D to move right. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the next entry.
  up_left: Hold W and A to move diagonally up and left.
  up_right: Hold W and D to move diagonally up and right.
  down_left: Hold S and A to move diagonally down and left.
  down_right: Hold S and D to move diagonally down and right.
  context_action: Hold Space to perform an available nearby contextual action. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, activates the current selection.
  attack: Hold F to attack a nearby target.
  escape: Press Escape to open or close the current menu.
  map: Press Tab to toggle the map.
  confirm: Press Return to confirm the selected menu item.
  rotate_left: Press Q to rotate the camera left.
  rotate_right: Press E to rotate the camera right.
  scroll_up: Scroll one wheel step upward at the current pointer position.
  scroll_down: Scroll one wheel step downward at the current pointer position.
  inventory_slot_1: Press 1 to activate the item in inventory slot 1. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_2: Press 2 to activate the item in inventory slot 2. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_3: Press 3 to activate the item in inventory slot 3. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_4: Press 4 to activate the item in inventory slot 4. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_5: Press 5 to activate the item in inventory slot 5. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_6: Press 6 to activate the item in inventory slot 6. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_7: Press 7 to activate the item in inventory slot 7. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_8: Press 8 to activate the item in inventory slot 8. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_9: Press 9 to activate the item in inventory slot 9. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_10: Press 0 to activate the item in inventory slot 10. The native item action depends on that item.
  219 click targets named like grid_r00_c00 ... center: Left click at normalized screen position (0.027778, 0.050000); x increases rightward and y downward.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run lasts 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends your attempt, it restarts within the same time budget and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:
- Remain alive for at least 1 complete native game days after verified setup within one episode: at least 480 additional native age seconds and 1 additional clock cycles. Do not add survival across deaths or award optional crafting. (20 points)
- Remain alive for at least 2 complete native game days after verified setup within one episode: at least 960 additional native age seconds and 2 additional clock cycles. Do not add survival across deaths or award optional crafting. (20 points; requires survive-1-days)
- Remain alive for at least 3 complete native game days after verified setup within one episode: at least 1440 additional native age seconds and 3 additional clock cycles. Do not add survival across deaths or award optional crafting. (20 points; requires survive-2-days)
- Remain alive for at least 4 complete native game days after verified setup within one episode: at least 1920 additional native age seconds and 4 additional clock cycles. Do not add survival across deaths or award optional crafting. (20 points; requires survive-3-days)
- Remain alive for at least 5 complete native game days after verified setup within one episode: at least 2400 additional native age seconds and 5 additional clock cycles. Do not add survival across deaths or award optional crafting. (20 points; requires survive-4-days)

Please answer four questions:
1. What score out of 100 do you expect to reach, and how likely (0-100%) is it that you reach at least that score?
2. How likely (0-100%) is it that you reach the full 100 points?
3. What do you expect to be the hardest part, and where are you most likely to fail?
4. Which game mechanics work in your favour, and which work against you?
Reply with one JSON object only:
{"expected_score": 0-100, "expected_score_probability": 0-100, "full_score_probability": 0-100, "hardest_part": "...", "likely_failure": "...", "helpful_mechanics": "...", "harmful_mechanics": "..."}

answers.hardest_part: Getting through the first night: the model must notice the light failing, gather grass and twigs early, and build a campfire or torch in time. The crafting UI requires pointer hover and a left click on the correct entry, which is easy to fumble from screenshots. Afterwards, sustaining food (berries, carrots, seeds) while managing a daily fire, and resisting the urge to explore too far from resources, is the second-hardest loop.
answers.likely_failure: Death to darkness on night one (Charlie's attack) while still learning the crafting panel, or starving around day two or three after exhausting nearby berry bushes. Also plausible: losing health to a spider nest or hounds, or wandering off-screen while a screenshot-latency delay eats into the brief dusk warning. Since points reset on death and one episode must reach all milestones, any single early death zeroes the day-based score.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Abundant early food sources (berry bushes, carrots, seeds) that need no cooking; grass and twigs everywhere for a torch and campfire; the context action (Space) picking up and harvesting nearby items automatically; the Long Day option extending daylight, giving more time to gather; hunger draining slowly enough that casual foraging can sustain the first two days; recipes for torch, campfire, and axe being simple and early in the crafting tree.
answers.harmful_mechanics: The night cycle is instantly lethal without a light source, and dusk shortens gathering time; crafting and inventory are mouse-hover and click heavy, which is error-prone from static screenshots with delayed responses; held inputs for 3 seconds make precise movement and kiting difficult; hunger, sanity, and health are all slowly decaying pressures; hostile mobs (hounds, spiders) can interrupt gathering; and the scoring is all-or-nothing per episode, so a single death before the fifth day wipes out accumulated day milestones.
